title: I Let the AirBnB House Manual Apply to the Host

parts.text: I followed the twelve-page checkout list and watched the host skip her own trash rule. I am twenty-nine, nurse on a rare weekend off, rented cabin energy in a city condo. The host, Blair, wanted the dishwasher run, towels in a spiral, vacuum lines in the rug. I did it. I even photographed the vacuum lines, sad little rows. She arrived early while I still had a suitcase on the bed. She dumped her McDonald's bag in the bin she said guests could not use. Blair said, "You're not supposed to be here still" I said, "Checkout is 11. It's 10:40" The bin liner was a specific lavender scent, aggressive. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened. I noticed a scuff on the floor shaped like a comma, which fit i. Someone had left a receipt in the cup holder, faded blue ink. The air tasted like leftover rain and cleaning spray, which fit i. A cheap clock on the wall jumped a minute late, then caught up. I kept my keys in my left pocket so I would not fidget, which fit i. The plastic chair stuck to my legs when I shifted. A vending machine hummed in another room like a bored insect, which fit i.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She is eating fries in the unit at 10:40 and the bin she banned is full of her trash.

parts.text: I stayed until 11, then sent the house-manual PDF with highlights and the fry photo. Blair threatened the deposit over 'attitude.' Airbnb support asked for the timestamps. Vacuum lines and 10:40 fries are timestamps with grease. The deposit came back. I reviewed factually. She replied with a novel. I went back to work and ate hospital cafeteria fries, worse, honest. The spiral towels were a fever dream. I will never spiral a towel again unless paid. Rare weekends should not include rug choreography. Support said, "Was checkout 11" Blair said, "They had an attitude" My coworker asked if the cabin fixed me. It was a condo. I said the vacuum lines almost did.
